questions.question: Before servicing a gas-fired appliance with electrical controls, what is the safest first action?
options: Lock out energy sources and verify zero energy
questions.explanation: Gas and electrical energy must be isolated before service. Lockout prevents accidental start-up, shock, gas release, or burner operation.

questions.question: A manometer is mainly used to measure:
questions.explanation: A manometer measures low gas pressure, often in inches of water column. It is commonly used for inlet and manifold pressure checks.

questions.category: A — Task 3: Plans and prepares work
questions.question: A job drawing and manufacturer instructions disagree on appliance clearance. What should the gasfitter do?
options: Ignore both and use judgment only
Follow the more restrictive approved requirement or clarify with authority
questions.explanation: Appliance clearances affect fire safety and service access. Manufacturer instructions, code, and AHJ requirements must all be satisfied.

questions.category: B — Task 4: Fits tube and tubing
questions.question: When bending soft copper tubing, the main concern is to avoid:
questions.explanation: Kinked tubing restricts gas flow and can weaken the tubing. Bends must be smooth and properly supported.

questions.question: Plastic gas pipe is commonly restricted from use:
options: Above ground inside buildings unless specifically approved
questions.explanation: Plastic gas piping has strict location and protection rules. It is commonly used underground but not freely inside buildings.
